clue.text: Progressive footballers

definitions.meaning: moving ahead, going onward in the direction faced
the attacking players in a football or rugby side, the strikers up front

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the word: an adverb of onward motion, and the attacking players up front in a team.

clue.text: It's in the forefront of architecture

definitions.text: It's in the forefront of architecture

parts.words: It's in the forefront of architecture
parts.note: read literally: the thing standing at the very front of a building, its principal face

explanation.surface: A remark about what leads the way in building design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forefront' sounds like leading fashion in design, but it means the literal front of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The front face of a building is its principal elevation, the part placed literally in front.

clue.text: Strip here for the take-off

parts.note: 'strip' is a landing strip and 'take-off' an aircraft leaving the ground, not undressing for a parody

explanation.surface: A notice inviting someone to undress before a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests undressing and a send-up; really it is the strip of tarmac aircraft leave from.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfield's paved strip is where aircraft accelerate and leave the ground.

clue.text: Semi-revolution in the ranks

parts.note: a half turn performed by soldiers on parade, not a partial uprising among them

explanation.surface: A half-hearted mutiny brewing among the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests revolt; here it is half a rotation, the parade-ground drill of turning to face the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A military drill command making soldiers turn round to face the opposite way, a half rotation.

clue.text: What makes Andrew wetter In Cumbria

definitions.text: What makes Andrew wetter In Cumbria

indicators.note: the letters of the two names makes something new when rearranged, signalling the reshuffle

explanation.surface: Asking what it is in the rainy Lake District that soaks poor Andrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' signals the anagram of ANDREW WETTER; the whole clue also defines, since a lake in Cumbria would indeed make Andrew wetter.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known lake in the English Lake District, in the county of Cumbria; falling in leaves one wet.

clue.text: There are signs of it in the sky

definitions.text: There are signs of it in the sky

parts.words: There are signs of it in the sky
parts.note: 'signs' are the twelve astrological star signs, not omens or clues spotted overhead

explanation.surface: Someone noticing hints of something overhead, like weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signs of it' sounds like evidence; it means the twelve star signs that make up the belt.
explanation.definitionFit: The belt of the heavens divided into twelve astrological constellations, each one a sign.

clue.text: This award is nothing to Mark

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that a prize means nothing compared to some man called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette of the film industry goes by this nickname.

clue.text: Peace move in press could be nice

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, signalling that the letters sit inside

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: could be says the letters of nice may become another arrangement

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a conciliatory gesture in the newspapers might be pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the fodder and 'in' sets the result inside. 'Press' looks like the newspapers but means smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal or writing aimed at reconciliation, especially between churches, is a conciliatory offering.

clue.text: Coy nurse maybe, but most attractive

indicators.note: maybe hints the words Coy and nurse are one possible order of the letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shy nurse might be the most attractive person on the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals an anagram of COY NURSE. The definition is loose: the answer is the most attractive thing, the centre of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre of attention or admiration, the thing that draws every eye, like a guiding star.

clue.text: Outlines study duty spells

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
tours are spells of duty, as in a tour of duty

explanation.surface: Someone sketching out how to study and how to work shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study is an old word for poring over or learning something.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines on a map tracing shape, or the general shape of anything, are its profiles.

clue.text: Project a picture of a riddle

definitions.meaning: to show a film or image on a surface
a riddle is also a coarse sieve, as a verb to sift through it

explanation.definitionFit: Showing a film is to put it on view; a coarse sieve, or riddle, separates soil or gravel by size.

clue.text: Drink in an East Anglian stable ?

definitions.text: Drink in an East Anglian stable ?

parts.words: Drink in an East Anglian stable
parts.note: a hot drink served in a Suffolk barn, but the stable houses a horse breed named after that county

explanation.surface: Wondering what beverage is served in a farm stable in eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: A heavy chestnut draught horse bred in the county of Suffolk, in East Anglia; its name also reads as a drink from that county.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of heavy draught horse from eastern England, so it lives in a stable there.

clue.text: Did business at the card table

definitions.text: Did business at the card table

parts.words: Did business at the card table
parts.note: doing business as a trader, or handing out the cards round a table

explanation.surface: Merchants striking deals over a card table.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both traded and gave out the cards for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader traded; a card player distributed the hands, both expressed by one past tense.

clue.text: Did these attendants get princely salaries?

definitions.text: Did these attendants get princely salaries?

parts.words: Did these attendants get princely salaries
parts.note: royal household officers who attend a prince, so the question asks whether their pay was fit for a prince

explanation.surface: A question about whether royal servants were richly paid.
explanation.walkthrough: They are officers attending members of the royal family; 'princely' means both lavish and to do with a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers of the British royal household who personally attend the monarch or a prince.

clue.text: Hard-wearing hardware by mail order ?

parts.note: 'mail' is chain mail and the hardware is metal worn on the body, not goods sent by post

explanation.surface: Durable tools bought from a catalogue through the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail order' suggests postal shopping; mail here is armour of linked rings, and the 'hardware' is literally hard to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete set of metal body protection worn by a knight, made partly of chain mail.

clue.text: About to go above North, climbing with fresh vitality

indicators.note: in a down entry, going above another piece means being placed before it

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an ascent is a climbing

explanation.surface: Instructions for a revived climber heading north on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go above' is a down-clue positional: the first piece sits above, that is before, the next in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reborn or springing up anew means having renewed life and energy.

clue.text: Peter and Paul get a job with the French

parts.note: a post is a job or position
les is the French plural article

explanation.surface: Two men named Peter and Paul land work together in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter and Paul look like any two men, but they are saints among Jesus's chosen twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints Peter and Paul are the foremost of the early Christian missionaries, both counted among the twelve.

clue.text: I ran hard all over the place to get the old vixen

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone running hard in every direction to escape a fierce old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' signals an anagram of I RAN HARD. Vixen is a female fox and, figuratively, a shrewish woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered, scolding old woman is a shrew; vixen is another word for such a termagant.

clue.text: Easy progress of a land-yacht

parts.note: smooth going in general, but literally a sail-driven land vehicle gliding across flat open country

explanation.surface: A wind-powered buggy bowling smoothly along.
explanation.walkthrough: An idiom for smooth, trouble-free progress, read literally as sailing across flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means straightforward progress without difficulty, originally sailing in clear water.

clue.text: European language could be French

definitions.meaning: French is a kind of shine for wood, the high-gloss finish on furniture

explanation.definitionFit: The national tongue of Poland; and French varnishing is a type of glossy finish for furniture.

clue.text: One is not sorry to be without it

definitions.text: One is not sorry to be without it

parts.words: One is not sorry to be without it
parts.note: lacking this feeling means having no remorse, so one feels no sorrow

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is glad to be rid of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests relief at losing an item; it means one without this feeling has nothing to be sorry about.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorrow or remorse over something done; having none means feeling no sorrow.

clue.text: Pile-up on the battlefield ?

parts.note: a heap of junk, but a scrap is also a fight, so a battlefield heap

explanation.surface: A heap of wrecked vehicles after a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: A pile of discarded material; 'scrap' as slang for a fight makes it the pile from a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of discarded metal and rubbish, figuratively where useless things end up.

clue.text: This meal is taken bit by bit

definitions.text: This meal is taken bit by bit

parts.words: This meal is taken bit by bit
parts.note: the word joined to 'meal' gives a phrase for gradually, a bit at a time

explanation.surface: A dish eaten slowly, morsel by morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the answer in front of 'meal' and you get the word meaning bit by bit; the answer itself means a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit or portion, which joined to 'meal' forms the adverb for gradually, one part at a time.

clue.text: Singular canonization of some weight

parts.note: canonization makes someone a saint, abbreviated St
singular means just one

explanation.surface: A remark on the gravity of making one person a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: A unit of weight of fourteen pounds, still used in Britain for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A British unit of fourteen pounds, used for people's body weight.

clue.text: Females first to pursue mother with complaints

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Females first to pursue mother with complaints' (6) for LADIES: no parse found giving L-A-D-I-E-S from 'first to pursue mother with complaints'; scan confirms the text, so the wordplay cannot be explained honestly.
annotationWithheld.clue: Females first to pursue mother with complaints

clue.text: One possibly finer-or less so

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of finer and or may come in another order

explanation.surface: Comparing two things, one perhaps better, or perhaps less good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns the fodder into NFERIOR after the numeral. 'less so' is the definition: not so fine, read against the clue's own 'finer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower in quality or rank, the opposite of finer, so less good.

clue.text: Moody companion in hymnology

parts.note: Dwight Moody, the American evangelist, partnered a gospel singer who compiled their famous hymn books

explanation.surface: A sulky partner in a church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: Moody looks like an adjective, sulky; it is Dwight L. Moody, whose evangelical partner Ira D. compiled the Victorian 'Moody and ...' hymnbooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ira D. Sankey, the American gospel singer, toured with evangelist Moody and compiled their hymn collections.

clue.text: Conversation of little note

parts.note: idle talk of no importance, with a pun on a chit being a short written note

explanation.surface: Talk about nothing in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: Trivial talk is 'of little note'; a chit is literally a little note.
explanation.definitionFit: Light, inconsequential talk or gossip is small talk.
